findings.claim: On a restart, a hung or unhealthy flusher is never killed. The new guard `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False for spawn-context processes, so `kill()` is skipped. The replacement then starts on the same shards and takes over the same process_healthy_since slot, which leaves the old process unmonitored. Two flushers can then flush the same segments, and up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS orphaned processes can pile up per index. The base code called kill() unconditionally.
findings.evidence: Processes come from multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, which creates a SpawnProcess with MRO (SpawnProcess, BaseProcess, object). The orchestrator ran `python3 -I -c "import multiprocessing as mp; p=mp.get_context('spawn').Process(target=print); print(isinstance(p, mp.Process))"`, which prints False. SP rated this Critical; OCR, PT and MP rated it Important.
findings.reason: Confirmed by an executed repro. It is a regression: the base code called kill() unconditionally. Fix: check multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess, or check for threading.Thread first. Red test: drive _ensure_processes_alive with a stale healthy_since and assert the old process is no longer alive.

findings.claim: When the deadline expires in join(), `break` skips terminate() for the current process and all later ones, so flushers from the old assignment can outlive a rebalance. `process_index` is unused, and the remaining_time check duplicates the inner while-loop's deadline check. The terminate() at line 346 uses the same wrong isinstance(multiprocessing.Process) check, which was already broken on base and is now copied into the per-process loop.
findings.evidence: Lines 337-341 do `remaining_time = deadline - time.time(); if remaining_time <= 0: break` before the wait and terminate, and line 346 is `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()`. Reasoned from the code. Uses the same isinstance repro as the kill finding.
findings.reason: OCR rated it Important; SP and PT rated it Minor. Once the isinstance guard is fixed, this becomes a real leak at shutdown. Fix: drop the early break so every process reaches terminate(), and correct the isinstance class.

findings.claim: Each process gets its own SpansBuffer covering only a subset of shards. Because SpansBuffer.flush_segments computes the per-shard limit as ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards)), the global option spans.buffer.max-flush-segments becomes a per-process budget. Total flush per cycle and the any_shard_at_limit backpressure threshold therefore both grow by a factor of the process count, and this is not documented.
findings.evidence: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:382-384,410; option doc at src/sentry/options/defaults.py:2716 says 'per cycle'. Reasoned, not executed. No change with the CLI default of 1, but it applies whenever max_processes > 1 or is None.
findings.reason: There is no spec stating this semantic change is intended. Either divide the budget across processes or document the new per-process meaning. Red test: with 2 processes and max-flush-segments=N, assert that at most N segments are flushed per cycle.

findings.claim: The defaults disagree. SpanFlusher and ProcessSpansStrategyFactory default max_processes to None (one process per shard), while the CLI default is 1 (one process for all shards). test_basic and test_backpressure leave the argument out, so they exercise the per-shard path, and the production configuration with multiple shards is untested.
findings.reason: SP rated it Important; PT rated it Minor. Pick one default (1, which matches base behaviour) everywhere, so the existing tests cover the production configuration.

findings.claim: No test covers the restart/kill path or flushing across multiple processes. The new test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts internals (max_processes, num_processes, processes, process_to_shards_map) and never checks that segments from all 4 shards are flushed. This gap is how the isinstance kill bug got through.
findings.evidence: test_consumer.py:84-123 produces no spans and asserts nothing about messages. Nothing calls _ensure_processes_alive. This breaches the user's 'test contracts, not implementation' rule (global CLAUDE.md, not a repo standard).
findings.reason: SP rated it Important; OCR, PT and MP rated it Minor. Replace the internals assertions with a behavioural check that 4 partitions all flush, and add a restart-path test. That test doubles as the red test for the kill finding.

findings.claim: The docstring 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing' is wrong for the default deployment, where the CLI default of 1 runs all shards in one process. The comments at lines 178 and 235 also don't match their code, since health is tracked per process, not per shard.
findings.reason: Docs that contradict the code. Correct the docstring and comments.

findings.claim: submit() now calls get_memory_info() (INFO on every node) and record_stored_segments() once per per-process buffer, even though every buffer talks to the same Redis cluster. That is N times the round trips on the consumer's main thread for no new information. The used/available ratio is unchanged because both sums scale by N.
findings.evidence: flusher.py:269-270 and 299-301 loop over self.buffers. SpansBuffer.get_memory_info is iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client) against the shared SENTRY_SPAN_BUFFER_CLUSTER (buffer.py:117).
findings.reason: Redundant I/O on the hot path. Call it once, for example by keeping the original full-shard buffer in the parent.

findings.claim: _create_process_for_shard is dead code: nothing in src/ or tests/ calls it.
findings.evidence: Grepping src/ and tests/ finds only the definition. Restarts go through _create_process_for_shards at line 259.

findings.claim: The `if not process: continue` guard in _ensure_processes_alive can never fire, because self.processes only holds started Process or Thread objects, and those are always truthy.
findings.evidence: flusher.py:124 is the only writer to self.processes.

findings.claim: The metric tag key is inconsistent: 'shards' at line 199 but 'shard' at lines 185, 195 and 244. The value is sometimes a comma-joined shard list and sometimes an int, and the joined lists change on every rebalance, which raises tag cardinality. buffer.py:371 uses 'shard_i' for the same concept.
findings.reason: Inconsistent metric tags break dashboards and queries. Use one key consistently.

findings.claim: The added `time.sleep(0.1)`, commented 'Give flusher threads time to process', does nothing, because line 15 monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op for the whole test. The race the comment describes is not addressed.
findings.reason: Misleading dead test code. Remove it, or wait on a real condition.

findings.claim: --flusher-processes is a plain int with no lower bound. A value of 0 silently means one process per shard. A negative value gives num_processes < 0, an empty process_to_shards_map and a KeyError from `i % n`.
findings.evidence: flusher.py:51,60 `max_processes or len(...)`, then `min(max_processes, len(...))`. Reasoned, not executed.
findings.reason: Input validation at the CLI boundary. Use click.IntRange(min=1).

findings.claim: The added hasattr/isinstance anti-pattern guidance has nothing to do with the span-flusher change and is scope creep in this PR.
findings.reason: The content is fine, but it belongs in its own PR. Drop it from this one.

findings.claim: max_processes is normalised twice (`max_processes or len(...)` and then `min(...)`), self.max_processes is kept only for the test, and _create_processes is a 2-line wrapper with one caller.
findings.reason: Advisory simplification with no behavioural impact. ponytail: collapse into a local n = min(max_processes or len(shards), len(shards)) once the default is unified.

findings.claim: Several new comments restate the code (lines 59, 82, 92, 241 and 336).
findings.reason: Advisory style finding. ponytail: remove the redundant comments during the fix round. The incorrect ones are covered by the docstring finding.

findings.claim: The switch to django_db(transaction=True) in test_basic and test_backpressure is unexplained.
findings.reason: No defect is claimed. transaction=True is the standard pytest-django requirement when code running in other threads or processes must see committed DB state, which is what the multi-process flusher introduces.

findings.claim: With no assigned shards, no flusher process starts (range(0)), whereas before an idle flusher process started anyway.
findings.reason: Both seats called it harmless. With no shards there is nothing to flush, and the liveness and backpressure loops iterate over an empty dict without error.
